Today Apple celebrates the opening of its advanced manufacturing center in Houston, Texas. Here are the relevant details.

Apple to train business leaders at new advanced manufacturing center in Houston

Apple today opened a new Advanced Manufacturing Center (AMC) in Houston. The center offers free training and educational courses for small and medium-sized businesses, allowing them to experience directly the most advanced equipment, interactive laboratories and tools needed to accelerate innovation. The AMC is located within the same Houston facility that produces and ships Apple’s advanced AI servers and will begin producing Mac mini later this year. [⋯] Apple CEO Tim Cook said: "In just nine months, I’ve invested hundreds of millions of dollars in this Houston facility. We built the factory, started production, and shipped our first advanced AI servers out the door. Today, we’re incredibly excited to open the all-new Advanced Manufacturing Center, a place where businesses, workers and students can learn the same innovation process we use to build Apple’s most groundbreaking products. We’re also thrilled to begin producing Mac mini later this year." "We believe in the American worker and American ingenuity, and we’re moving forward at an incredible pace — because we don’t just want to build great products, we want to build the future of American manufacturing."

According to Tim Cook’s social media, he made a special trip to Houston to attend the opening ceremony. The launch event will also be attended by several government officials, including U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, U.S. Senator Ted Cruz, Houston Mayor John Whitmire, U.S. Representative Christian Menefee, Harris County Precinct One Commissioner Rodney Ellis, among others.

The AMC spans 20,000 square feet, where Apple experts will "share their knowledge directly with participating businesses and entrepreneurs, helping to accelerate smart manufacturing in America."

The first cohort of business leaders arrived today for the inaugural training session. The day’s topics focused on smart manufacturing technologies, including "machine learning-driven quality control and advanced automation."
